turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start off, can you tell me what brought you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I'm having some issues at work. I'm an electrician, and I just keep going back over my jobs again and again. 

I'll check the breakers, make sure the labels are right, check the torque marks... I even take photos of the panel to look at later, or sometimes I actually drive all the way back to a site just to check it one more time. It's getting to the point where a simple install takes way, way longer than it should, and people are starting to notice. So I figured I should probably come talk to someone about it.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes excessive, repetitive checking behaviors at work, such as repeatedly verifying breakers, torque marks, taking photos of panels to re-examine, and driving back to job sites.

turns.doctor_question: When you go back to check the panels again, is it because a specific unwanted thought or fear—like 'what if I caused a fire' or 'what if something is wrong'—keeps popping into your mind and won't let you rest until you check?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, that's exactly what it is. Even after I know for a fact I checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought just keeps barging in on me. I'll start thinking, you know, maybe I missed one loose neutral wire, or maybe I left something in there that could start a fire. I try to shake it off, I really do, but it just... it follows me all the way home. It won't let up until I finally give in and go back to look at it again.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes intrusive, persistent thoughts about having missed a wire or causing a fire that barge in and that they actively try to shake off, confirming obsessions.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient reports repetitive checking behavior ('go back to look at it again') performed in response to the intrusive thoughts to relieve distress, confirming checking compulsions.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from the urge to go back and check, do you also find yourself dealing with these same intrusive thoughts—like worrying about a fire—at other times, even when you're not near a job site or about to check anything?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. It's pretty much just tied to my work. When I'm off the clock and at home, I'm not sitting around worrying about my own breaker box or anything like that. It's just the jobs I've done that day. Once I've checked them enough times to feel okay about it, the thoughts kind of stop. So, no, it's not really bothering me outside of work.

turns.doctor_question: On a typical day, about how many hours would you say you spend on this checking and re-checking behavior?
turns.patient_response: I'd say... maybe an hour or two a day? It kind of depends on how many jobs I had, but yeah, probably at least an hour just driving back or standing there staring at the panel, making sure it's right. Sometimes more if I really can't get the thought out of my head.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms engaging in time-consuming checking behaviors, spending an hour or two each day driving back or staring at the panel to ensure it is right.
